hook: Marines fired a rocket truck from the deck of a ship.
narration: Marines fired a rocket truck from the deck of a Navy ship.
This HIMARS sat on the flight deck of USS Anchorage.
[short pause] Its target was on land.
A HIMARS pod holds six rockets, and it reaches farther than ordinary artillery.
outcome: The rocket destroyed that target seventy kilometers away.
title: Rocket truck fires off a Navy ship
description:
Marines with Battery R, 5th Battalion, 11th Marine Regiment fire a High Mobility Artillery Rocket System (HIMARS) from the flight deck of USS Anchorage (LPD 23) at a land-based target during Exercise Dawn Blitz, Oct. 22, 2017.

Footage: U.S. Marine Corps video by Lance Cpl. Victoria Decker, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/561288/himars-launch-uss-anchorage

extra_sources.excerpt: PACIFIC OCEAN – The High Mobility Artillery Rocket System (HIMARS) was fired from the flight deck of the San Antonio-class amphibious transport dock ship USS Anchorage (LPD 23) during Dawn Blitz 2017, Oct. 22.
The HIMARS is a weapons system made up of the M142, five-ton chassis vehicle and can carry either a launcher pod of six rockets or one MGM-140 Army Tactical Missile System (ATACMS).

It enables Marines to engage targets within minutes after firing and features an advanced targeting system that strikes with an extremely high accuracy rate. The system also features a greater range than traditional artillery, allowing smaller units to cover a larger area.
The demonstration on Anchorage consisted of HIMARS engaging a land-based target with a Guided Multiple Launch Rocket System Unitary (GMLRS-U).
We achieved both objectives. We destroyed the target at 70 kilometers while at sea.
